assertions.assert: Each element (to_json, contents, cut_at_word, stm_projection) takes exactly its declared attributes, the required ones present and none empty, and no content, and the namespace has no other element: a malformed element raises error.execution and assigns nothing (its schema, package/memory.xsd, rejects it before any run under scx validate).

<memory:to_json> writes a message's memory JSON as one JSON text: {content, content_type, source_ids, target_ids} with sorted keys and compact separators, the content's arrays and objects tagged __stateforward_memory_content__ list and mapping (a mapping's entries ordered by their keys in code point order), every number as its JSON number, and the identities sorted without repeats, each embedding its JSON array; a message without identity arrays raises error.execution and assigns nothing.

<memory:contents> writes, in row order, the first value of each row of one statement's result that is a string holding a JSON object, parsed, and skips every other row; a result without a rows array raises error.execution and assigns nothing.

<memory:cut_at_word> writes {text, cut}: words of at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes unchanged and cut false; longer words cut, cut true, to their whole characters within the bound, less the partial word the bound falls inside when an earlier word break exists, trailing white space (Unicode White_Space) removed; words that are not a string raise error.execution and assign nothing.

<memory:stm_projection> writes the bounded scalar projection of a value: an object's fields in their order, keeping each with a non-empty key and a boolean, number, or string of at most 40 characters, at most 16 fields, every other field dropped, never truncated; a bare boolean, number or bounded string as {value}; anything else {}.
